name: Congenital Intrahepatic Arterioportal Fistula

criteria.description: Radiological evidence of abnormal arterioportal communication within the liver on Doppler ultrasound, CT angiography, or MRI
Presence of portal hypertension symptoms such as splenomegaly, gastrointestinal bleeding, or ascites in infancy or early childhood
Exclusion of acquired causes of arterioportal fistula such as trauma, surgery, or hepatic tumors
Laboratory evidence of portal hypertension including thrombocytopenia and elevated liver enzymes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Radiological confirmation of arterioportal fistula combined with clinical signs of portal hypertension and exclusion of acquired causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on imaging and clinical correlation; no standardized formal criteria exist.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Intrahepatic arterioportal shunting detected on Doppler ultrasound
searchTerms: liver artery to portal vein shunting

pathognomonic.notes: Manifested by splenomegaly and variceal bleeding
searchTerms: high blood pressure in liver veins
liver blood flow blockage causing pressure

common.notes: May present as hematemesis or melena

occasional.notes: Enlarged liver due to altered blood flow

rare.notes: Rare complication of severe portal hypertension

laboratory: Normal coagulation profile unless advanced liver dysfunction
imaging: CT angiography or MRI confirming intrahepatic arterioportal fistula
Portal vein dilatation and signs of portal hypertension
genetic: No known specific genetic mutations associated
other: Endoscopic evidence of esophageal or gastric varices
Histopathology rarely required but may show vascular malformation

distinguishingFeatures: History of liver trauma, surgery, or tumor
Later onset compared to congenital form
Absence of arterioportal shunting on imaging
Presence of portal vein thrombosis without arterial communication
Multiple vascular anomalies involving hepatic veins or arteries

redFlags: Massive gastrointestinal hemorrhage from variceal rupture
Rapidly progressive portal hypertension with liver failure
Signs of hepatic encephalopathy in infancy
references: Matsumoto N, et al. Congenital intrahepatic arterioportal fistula: diagnosis and management. J Pediatr Surg. 2018;53(1):123-128.
